blocks.text: This guide illustrates how to configure OneLogin as the identity provider (IdP) for the Zscaler service. It also describes how to integrate Active Directory and configure an AD connector. Refer to the OneLogin documentation for additional information about the steps in the example.
Ensure that you have the following before you start configuring OneLogin as the IdP:

blocks.item: A OneLogin account with admin privileges
The Zscaler SAML certificate (See Adding Identity Providers.)

blocks.heading: Configuring OneLogin as the IdP for the Zscaler service

blocks.text: To configure OneLogin as the IdP for the Zscaler service:

blocks.item: 1. Add the Zscaler Application in OneLogin
To add the Zscaler application to OneLogin:
Log in to OneLogin as an administrator.
Go to Portal, then click Find apps.
See image.
In the Find apps window, enter Zscaler in the search field, then click add next to the Zscaler application.
See image.
In the Add Zscaler window, choose Zscaler in the This app will be used by field.
Click Continue.
On the Single Sign-on tab, do the following, and then click Update:
SAML Endpoints URL: Copy the SAML Endpoints URL. You paste this in Step f of 6. Configure SAML SSO in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Credentials: Select Configured by admin.
Default values: Select Email for the NameID (Login).
See image.
2. Download the OneLogin SAML Certificate
To download the OneLogin SAML certificate:
Go to Security > SAML.
Under x.509 certificate, click .PEM format to download your IdP SAML SSL certificate in PEM format.
See image.
3. Assign Users to the Zscaler Application
You can assign users individually or by roles. This guide describes how to assign users by roles.
To assign users to the Zscaler application:
Go to People > Roles.
Click edit.
Select Zscaler from the list of apps.
Click Commit changes, then click Update.
4. Add an Active Directory Server
To add a new Active Directory (AD):
Go to People > Directories.
Click New Directory.
Click Windows Server Active Directory.
See image.
In the New Directory window, click Update.
In the Active Directory window, do the following, then click Update:
Download the AD connector.
Copy the token to your clipboard. You need it for step d in 5. Install the OneLogin Active Directory Connector.
See image.
When the confirmation message appears, click Save File.
5. Install the OneLogin Active Directory Connector
To install the OneLogin AD connector:
Start the AD connector.
When the wizard appears, click Next.
Specify where you’d like to install the connector and click Next.
In the Directory Token window, paste the token you copied in step e of 4. Add an Active Directory Server, then click Next.
See image.
Click Close.
If a proxy is in place within your network, create a proxy rule to allow the OneLogin AD connector traffic through the proxy.
6. Add OneLogin as the IdP for the Zscaler service
7. Configure SAML SSO in the Zscaler Admin Console
To configure SAML SSO in the Zscaler Admin Console:
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Internet & SaaS Authentication > Internet Authentication Settings > Default Settings.

Under Authentication Frequency, choose how often users are required to authenticate to the Zscaler service. To learn more, see About Authentication Default Settings. If you select Custom, the following field appears:
Custom Authentication Frequency (days): Specify 1 to 180 days.
Under Authentication Type, choose SAML.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
8. Configure the Zscaler Authentication Exemptions List
To configure the Zscaler Authentication Exemptions list and enable users access to OneLogin:
From the navigation menu, go to Internet Access > Setting > Advanced Settings.
In the Authentication Exemptions section, enter app.onelogin.com in Exempted URLs.
Click Save and activate the change.
If you're using PAC files, enter the following exception to the PAC file exemption list. Otherwise, the authentication fails.
If (shExpMatch(host, "app.onelogin.com")) return "DIRECT";

blocks.text: This testing method only applies if you're forwarding traffic using PAC files, GRE tunnels, or IPSec tunnels, and you've enabled Enforce Authentication for the location or sublocation.
To test the SAML configuration with OneLogin:

blocks.item: If you're already logged in to the Zscaler service, browse to https://login.<Zscaler cloud Name>/zscaler.portal, and click Logout. Replace <Zscaler cloud Name> with your Zscaler cloud name. To learn how you can find your cloud name, see Understanding Zscaler Cloud Names.
Ensure that your traffic is being forwarded to the Zscaler service and then browse to a website.
When prompted for authentication, enter your OneLogin credentials.

blocks.text: If any errors occur, see Troubleshooting SAML to troubleshoot browser settings and SAML error codes.
